newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMPLATS SEES RUSSIA'S NORILSK OUTPUT FLAT.
newsitem.headline: AMPLATS SEES RUSSIA'S NORILSK OUTPUT FLAT.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) said on Monday it did not expect major Russian producer Norilsk Nickel to increase platinum production significantly in the future.

Amplats commerical director Dorian Emmett told a South African mining conference organised by stockbrokers E.W. Balderson that the Russian firm had technical problems which was curtailing platinum production.
"All our information from Norilsk points that it is not going to be able to readily and significantly increase its production over the medium term.
"It has technical problems...it is going to be rather difficult for them to rely on a short-term basis on producing more," Emmett said.

Platinum refiner Johnson Matthey said in its latest annual platinum report that for Norilsk to maintain output in the longer term, significant investment was needed to develop replacement ore reserves and upgrade processing facilities.
Johnson Matthey said the investment was unlikely to be forthcoming while the ownership of the Russian company is in question.
Norilsk annual nickel output accounts for 20 percent of world supply, platinum for 23 percent and palladium for 60 percent.
